memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Make the tabernacle with ten curtains of finely twisted linen and blue, purple and scarlet yarn, with cherubim woven into them by a skilled worker. All the curtains are to be the same size — twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide." - Exodus 26:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God begins describing His dwelling place with curtains of finely twisted linen, woven with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and cherubim embroidered by skilled hands. He could have asked for something plain and functional — it was, after all, a tent in a desert. Instead He asked for beauty, made by craftsmen who knew their work.

This tells us something worth noticing. God is not indifferent to beauty. He made a world of colour and pattern, and when He specified His own dwelling, He asked for artistry. Skill, craftsmanship, and beauty are not distractions from spiritual life; they can be genuine offerings to God. The person who weaves well, builds well, or creates well is using something God-given.

There is also a quiet reminder here about excellence. These curtains were made carefully, to exact measurements, by people who had learned their craft. God honoured skill. Whatever your work — practical, creative, technical, or domestic — doing it well can be a way of honouring the God who gave you the ability. Paul tells us that whatever we do, we should work at it with all our heart, as for the Lord (Col 3:23). Bring your skill, however ordinary it seems, and use it for Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I see my skills and craftsmanship as gifts I can offer back to God?
Am I bringing genuine care and excellence to the work God has given me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are the source of every skill I have. Help me use my abilities with care and excellence, offering my work back to You as an act of worship. Amen.
